comment: Kaufman makes the content very interesting and relates it to modern-day issues. He can be a bit confusing sometimes, and his grading criteria is a little weird. To do well, you have to read.

Professor Kaufman may seem intimidating but he's extremely approachable, hilarious, and gives amazing feedback on your work. He is so intelligent that it's almost scary, and he makes lectures engaging. It's a tough course with lots of reading and high expectations for papers, but he is willing to dial the workload down if you ask.

Dr. Kaufman is by far my favorite professor I have had at Richmond. His lectures are incredibly interesting and have made me think of things with new perspectives. I have learned so much about politics and the world through his class. There are oral exams and papers but they have benefited me so much and are so much better than normal exams.
He is the best professor at Richmond, full stop. Take his class if you are actually interested in learning and are willing to put the work in.

One of the best professors I've ever had at the University of Richmond. An intellectual who will go out of his way, even outside of class, to hold meaningful discussions with his students about so many important topics or anything. A class format which is untraditional, but incredibly rewarding.

Professor Kaufman is one of the best professors I've had. He truly cares about his students and is very helpful. Office hours are great for clarifying assignments. Expect a lot of reading, though he may reduce it. I loved the oral exams—they let you collaborate and exchange ideas in small groups. There's no final exam, just papers.

TAKE THIS CLASS! Kaufman is the best prof I've had - cares really deeply about his students and is obviously brilliant and it shows in his lectures. Definitely a difficult class, but if you put in the effort you will learn so much and it will reflect in your grade. Heavy readings but he listens to student feedback and cuts them down if you ask.
Really interesting but get ready to be cold called multiple times every class. If you dont do the 100 page reading the day before youre done for.
Kaufman is a nice and interesting professor, but this was my least favorite class I've taken in college. It is not very engaging and the readings were long and extremely dense.

Awesome Professor, his class is extremely interactive and he clearly loves to teach. The readings are lengthy, but he is a wonderful professor. Different style of teaching compared to other 101 classes. GO TO OFFICE HOURS.

Kaufman is such a good prof. Most of the readings are interesting and the class time is spent talking about the books he wants to hear from you more than himself. A couple papers but if you go to his office hours he is very willing to discuss your grade.

Dr. Kaufman is one of the most fascinating men you'll ever meet. His take on LDST101 is basically a philosophy class, and his lectures is a part of the reason University of Richmond is regarded as such a good school. A little tough on grading, but go to his office hours. 100% would reccomend

Kaufman is that type of professor that you'll remember forever. He's funny, genuine, and cares about his students. All you need to do to pass is participate every class and then write five papers throughout the semester (800 words). You never take notes, you just need to participate. The reading can be a lot at times but it's all rlly interesting.

He is just the best. There is no other way to describe it. My favorite teacher I have ever taken literally ever. He wants to see you do well and wants you to be successful. His lectures and comments are hilarious and the 2 and a half hours goes by quickly with small group work and class discussions. Will never have to take a single note in class.

Dr. Kaufman is an amazing professor, who was a great introduction college. He is older, yet has the same energy as his own students. He brings immense knowledge and prospective to class discussions, and his life stories are not only crazy, but also hilarious. Kaufman's class is definitely reading heavy, which he warns you about, but 1000% worth it!

Kaufman is a fantastic professor. His classes are interesting even though lectures can be a little confusing. He genuinely cares about his students and wants to see them thrive. For example, he was my only professor this semester that took the time to remember where I'm from/what my major was/what field I want to go into. He's also really funny.

Kaufman is an amazing professor, and you can tell that he's really excited about what he teaches. He can be intimidating at first, but he's friendly and actually kind of hilarious. His lectures can be unclear sometimes, and his paper prompts can be even more unfocused, but the discussions in that class are really insightful, and I loved it.
Gives lots of readings and class relies on participation. Initially intimidating, but very funny and interesting. Go to his office hours to prep for the papers

I am in Dr. Kaufman's leadership 101 class at the moment and I absolutely love it. He warns you before the class starts that you should be ready for heavy reading, which we have often. He is absolutely hilarious and incredibly intelligent. This is my favorite class and I wish he taught more courses. If you are gonna take 101, take his class!

Very heavy on readings and participation. May seem mean at first, but he's a really interesting guy and can be really funny. Your grade depends on a few papers, so it's important to do all the readings. It is difficult but you can take a lot away from this class and be left with a better understanding of things.

Definitely intimidating at first, but once you get to know him, he's a nice, genuine guy who very clearly cares about students' education. If you are willing to put in the work (readings, etc.) he will respect you immensely and do everything he can to help you succeed. His class makes you think, and he doesn't spoon-feed, which I appreciated.
Dr. Kaufman is hysterical. Very intimidating at first but once he knows you're in for the long run. I enjoyed the class, material can be very dry but Kaufman makes it more fun.

This class is not a breeze. There is A LOT of reading involved and his class discussions will involve you knowing what's going on in the event he randomly calls on you. However, Kaufman is enlightening and funny (his mouth has no filter). I would 100% take his class again, he is by far the most entertaining professor, with an interesting background

Professor Kaufman is an amazing and quirky instructor that never fails to make me think about the topics that are discussed in class. His unique way of teaching the class allows the students to formulate their own opinions, rather than being spoon fed what is the "best" way to be a leader, or the best way to act in a situation.
why did i take this class

Dr. Kaufman is one of the most entertaining, quirky and genuine professors I have had in my time at Richmond. His lectures are engaging and class discussion is a huge part of this course. Don't expect an A but if you work hard there is no reason you won't do well.

Kaufman is my favorite professor at UR. He pushes you to be the best student you can be, but he wont take any bull sh*t so you have to focus and do the readings to do well. If you work hard, it will pay off. He's also a great person to have a conversation with outside of class. Awesome guy overall!

Fair warning: Kaufman wants his course to change you. So your participation in class sincerely matters to him. Approach every assignment searching for an accurate understanding (obviously), and note your personal reaction to the contents. But if you want more than a B, proactively refer to the handouts and syllabus.
Solid Professor, Glad I took him. Deserves the Pepper!
He was good

If you're not interested in the topic andor don't want to participate in class discussion, don't take his class. He's also very good with one-on-one and is happy to help you. He loves to see passionate students, whether they agree with his views or not

Kaufman is hilarious but the material for this class is dry, which he acknowledged. Course itself isn't too hard but he wants you to do the readings and have opinions on the subjects. There are no clear-cut answers for this class so as long as you can support you opinion with evidence he'll agree with you. If you try, he'll raise your grade

THE man. Kauffman word's ring throughout your head long after you've completed his class. Easy to talk to and truly loves what he does. One of the most interesting speakers I've ever had the pleasure of hearing. Don't worry about attendance because you are not going to want to miss class. TAKE HIS CLASS!!!
I loved going to his class. He was funny, interesting and a great lecturer. I would take his class again in a heartbeat.

Great guy.  Grades aren't often as they appear numerically.. (thankfully, because he tends to be tough).  Lots of reading.. and you really need to be up to date as this course is detail-oriented and confusing.

Kaufman is a great guy. He is super smart and loves what he teaches. Class can get pretty boring, and he gives pop quizzes on the readings which stink sometimes, but usually aren't too hard. He assigns a lot of reading, but you can get by without doing it for the most part. Easy 'B,' hard 'A'

Although he does love to hear himself talk, he's a great speaker and always interesting.  Valuable insight into the morals, challenges, and different categories of leaders.  A lot of reading but if you pay attention/participate in class discussions you can get by with skimming/sparknotes and still get a good grade.

I had never seen such a passionate professor. You think you read and understand an article, and as soon as you get to class he brings life to whatever topic you're doing. I promise you won't ever be bored in class. He incorporates tons of discussion into his "lectures" and he'll bring the best out of you. You'll leave his class with strong ideas.
Awesome teacher.. extremely talented and enthusiastic.

Easiest, most interesting class I've taken so far. As long as you do the readings and participate in class his quizzes and tests are easy. He is always energetic and light-hearted with the material, and it's obvious that he cares about his students and what he's teaching them. Would recommend his class to anyone interested in leadership at all.
Really great teacher the university should be proud to have him. While his quizzes are often hard and vague, the course material is truly interesting.

Very good teacher. Generally interested in the topic and his students comments and views.plans for time to be lost in class. Promotes class discussion daily so be prepared to talk. Used a total points system so you always know how you are doing and what your final grade may look like. only religious comment he had made is that he was not religious

do NOT take this class unless you love talking about your relationship with god every day.   don't be fooled, he's not a leadership professor, he's a religion professor.  great guy, really nice.  he thinks richmond kids are stupid so he's really impressed if you say a semi-intelligent comment.
Great teacher... Expects you to read everything that he assigns, which about 3 times more than your freshman core class.  Very Helpful, but the reading load is way to much.
Awesome teacher...very engaging and interested in what hes teaching...very very nice.  not out to get you at all. do the reading and you will do great.  best professor ive had in college
